title: Subagent frontmatter (subagent-v1)
$comment: Source: ADR-109. A subagent is an addressable, tool-scoped execution context projected to a host's native subagent format (Claude Code `.claude/agents/`) or, on non-subagent hosts, to a loadable context file. Static projection only — dispatch stays with the host/user, never runtime-enforced. Governance fields (trust, lifecycle, discovery.visible) are REQUIRED, mirroring the skill trust block so subagents share one governance model. model_tier reuses model_tier.ts (ADR-034/035).

name.description: Addressable handle. Must match the subagent filename stem and be globally unique within the subagent category (projection-path collision guard).

description.description: User-facing summary. On Claude Code this drives `@`-menu discoverability; keep it action-oriented.

model_tier.description: Vendor-neutral capability band (ADR-034/035, amended by ADR-232). frontier/high/medium/lite project to a native Claude `model:` via model_tier.ts; `inherit` is a documented passthrough sentinel (→ CC `model: inherit`), not a new mapping. `frontier` is the band above the strongest generally-recommended one - opt-in, expected to stay rare, and never the resolution of `inherit`.

effort.description: Optional pinned reasoning-effort level. Projects into the generated .claude/agents/<name>.md frontmatter (`effort:`) on hosts with an effort knob; ignored elsewhere. Orthogonal to `model_tier`. Omit for host-default effort.

tools.description: A tool grant: one of the Claude Code tool names, optionally scoped — `Bash(npm test:*)` grants one command family where a bare `Bash` grants a shell. The base name stays closed, so a typo still fails CI rather than producing broken `.claude/agents/` YAML in the user's IDE; only the optional `(...)` suffix is new. Prefer the narrowest grant the task actually needs, per tool-safety Least Agency.
tools.$comment: Was a bare enum, which made the scoped-grant syntax `tool-safety` prescribes literally inexpressible here — a schema forbidding what the rule asks for. skill.schema.json's allowed_tools permits that syntax by validating nothing at all; this pattern permits it while keeping the base-name guarantee that made the enum worth having.

trust.description: ADR-013 trust block, mirrored from the skill schema so subagents share one governance model.

visible.description: Subagents are default-off. The value MUST be false; a pack/profile opts in explicitly via include: ["subagent:<name>"].

requires_capability.description: Host-capability gate (e.g. claude_subagents). Hosts without the capability receive the loadable-context-file degradation, not native dispatch.

role.description: What the definition is for, declared rather than inferred from its name or description. `judge` covers every definition that judges, reviews, validates or audits another agent's work; a `judge` MUST declare `reuse: never` (judge Iron Law), enforced by validate_frontmatter and read by the reuse decision in `_lib/worker_reuse.ts`.
role.$comment: Release-17 finding 8851a226345a: the judge-never-reusable invariant used to rest on a /judge|review|validat|audit/ regex over name and description, so a judging agent described differently stayed reusable.

reuse.description: Freshness class, declared rather than inferred. `continuity` lets a finished worker be re-tasked when every condition in `_lib/worker_reuse.ts` holds; `never` means every dispatch is fresh — required of every judge, reviewer and validator (judge Iron Law). Read off the source definition; never projected, because the host has no per-definition reuse key.

omit_project_instructions.description: Skip the project instruction hierarchy for this worker. Projects to the host's skip flag; ships unset on every definition until step 2.5's net-delta reading and its kernel-and-constraints fixture both hold.

preload_skills.description: Skills whose full body the host injects at every cold start. Each one is paid per spawn, so add one only on a paired measurement showing the worker needs it on almost every run.

max_turns.description: Upper bound on agentic turns per run. Projects to the host's turn cap.

background.description: Run the worker in the background by default. Projects to the host's background flag.

cache_ttl.description: Prompt-cache TTL the worker's reuse decision reads as condition (b). Ships unset (host default) on every definition — decision D7: a one-hour write is spend, taken only on a measured re-task gap distribution. Not projected: the host's TTL knob is a settings value, not a per-definition key.
